project_scope.note: B030 split under current Kew taxonomy: bushy bluestem and broomsedge move to Anatherum; familiar Andropogon names remain aliases.

study_strategy.warning: Do not identify these grasses from fall color alone. The inflorescence architecture is the fastest reliable split.

quick_split: Andropogon gerardi — tall prairie grass with 2–6 exposed digitate racemes, often a turkey-foot.
Anatherum glomeratum — dense broad fluffy/broomlike clusters near the top.
Anatherum virginicum — narrower silky racemes partly tucked inside flattened spathe-like sheaths.
comparison_lesson.caveat: Older Texas floras place all three familiar plants in Andropogon; the learner keeps those aliases searchable while displaying the current accepted Kew names.
